comments.text: Wonderful video. I have seen Pasolini's Gospel According to Matthew twice. I knew it was filmed in Matera, which I have also visited twice. One thing I could not understand: where did Pasolini film it? Thank you for explaining the clearance of the sassi and removal of the people. So Pasolini made his film in the time interval when the sassi were uninhabited.  Thank you also for the details of the Messina earthquake. I didn't know that Reggio also was hit, and about the huge tidal wave. I was in Lecce, and a friend lives in Messina. I called him and said: Hey, let's meet halfway.  Absolutely not, he replied, and furthermore, under no circumstances should you stop in Calabria. That was the period of the kidnappings. Puglia is wonderful I love Puglia. Ostuni, Bari, Brindisi, Monopoli and so on, but the most beautiful in my opinion is Trani. Thank you for the interesting video.

replies.text: What a lovely thread of memories, thank you for sharing it. Your point about Pasolini is a fascinating way to see it, the Sassi becoming a film set just as one chapter of the city was closing. For anyone who knows Puglia well, does Trani get your vote too, or is there a town you'd put above it?
